elements.text: In-flight cargo fire of undetermined origin
Flightcrew properly certificated and qualified
No behavioral or psychological factors related to fatigue affected the flightcrew
Smoke detection system functioned as intended
Air traffic controllers responded appropriately
Airplane was properly certificated, equipped, and maintained
No evidence of systems, mechanical, or structural failures
Flight engineer’s failure to pull the cabin air shutoff T-handle
Continuing circulation of air providing oxygen to the fire
Rapid growth of the fire
Evacuation delayed because flightcrew failed to ensure proper depressurization
Captain did not adequately manage crew resources
Captain failed to call for checklists
Captain failed to monitor and facilitate checklist items
Crewmembers not using protective breathing equipment
Crewmembers unaware that opening pressurized exit doors may result in failure to open
DNA synthesizer not completely purged of volatile chemicals before transport
Presence of aerosol cans, acidic liquids, and marijuana on board
Common carriers unaware of true content of packages
Transportation of undeclared hazardous materials remains a significant problem
DOT hazardous materials regulations do not adequately address retrievability of information
FedEx’s policy of providing information only after investigation initiation
Need for more effective preparation for hazardous materials emergencies
Need for coordination among Air National Guard, airport management, and emergency agencies
Airport emergency plans should address hazardous materials emergencies
Inadequate means exist for extinguishing on-board aircraft fires
Aircraft rescue and firefighting capabilities must be improved
